gate.bootstrap_runtime_guide.description: Require a fresh guide surface from the selected published SO runtime before any downstream review or authoring work.

failureGuidance.summary: The selected runtime did not yield a fresh guide result before the work continued.
failureGuidance.nextAction: Run so.exe --guide on Windows or so --guide on Unix from the extracted package. Verify the returned version and readable guide paths before retrying.

evidenceReferences.quote: A fresh `so[.exe] --guide` or `ao[.exe] --guide` call is the first runtime operation after extraction.

gate.compile_review_ready.description: Compile-review gate for AO governance enhancement template.

failureGuidance.summary: Compile-review evidence is missing or the generated Mermaid, HTML, and analysis artifacts do not describe the current workflow.
failureGuidance.nextAction: Dispatch the workflow designer, repair the authoritative template, rerun the direct SO apphost compile, and return fresh workflow_mermaid_md, workflow_html, workflow_analysis_json, workflow_dataflow_json, and workflow_compile_feedback before continuing.

evidenceReferences.quote: - For every full-delivery enhancement or re-enhancement of a Loom-governanced skill being enhanced, `the direct SO apphost compile` is never an end state. It is only a validation checkpoint and one boundary-check precondition.

gate.official_blocked.description: Strongest runtime-owned blocked-boundary evidence gate for the official runnable route.

failureGuidance.summary: The blocked runtime boundary lacks its same-instance workflow copy or event log.
failureGuidance.nextAction: Preserve the runtime-owned workflow copy and event log for the same external workflow instance before attempting recovery.

evidenceReferences.quote: - If `run` returns a runtime-owned block, pass that boundary check and continue with `the direct SO apphost resume` against that exact workflow copy and persisted state. If the runtime reports a recoverable failure, preserve its evidence and resume from the previous state on the same persisted copy. Repeat until final `Done`; a blocked payload alone is never a terminal outcome and never approval to skip the next gate. Stop only when the failed instance has no recoverable previous state or the official runtime cannot start, and preserve that failure evidence.

gate.official_done.description: Terminal gate for official runnable route to final Done.

failureGuidance.summary: Completion remains blocked: the selected SO runtime exposes no verified producer for the target completion manifest or terminal business evidence; a completed runtime status is not business completion.
failureGuidance.nextAction: Keep the route blocked. Add and test an authorized manifest producer and independent terminal-evidence validator before enabling this gate; never infer or fabricate these outputs.

evidenceReferences.quote: - After direct apphost guide validation and guide handoff, create or reuse one fresh external runtime workflow instance copy and record its immutable instance identity, workflow-file path, and persisted runtime-state/session path. Run `the direct SO apphost compile` against that exact external copy, pass the compile-boundary check, then immediately dispatch the public `the direct SO apphost run` against the same copy. Every later `the direct SO apphost resume` must reference the same persisted instance and state; never switch to a new workflow copy between compile, run, or a block. Do not stop at a preflight explanation, local geometry/tool validation, a draft workflow, compile output, or a blocked-state description when the user has required execution.

gate.replan_history_ready.description: Blocked-route history gate proving the planner received the current state, blocker, attempts, outcomes, and evidence before redesign.

failureGuidance.summary: The replan history gate lacks the current blocker, prior attempts, outcomes, or audit evidence required for a grounded redesign.
failureGuidance.nextAction: Record the current blocker and every attempted path in replan_history and attempt_history, attach blocker_report and audit_artifacts, then retry.

evidenceReferences.quote: The references must point to the specific contract, guide, target `SKILL.md`, workflow source, or artifact instruction that explains how to repair this gate. Absolute paths, estimated line numbers, directory-only citations, bare filenames, and paraphrases in place of quoted source are invalid. A failed gate must leave the next agent with enough information to act without rediscovering the governing rule.

gate.replan_path_ready.description: Replan gate proving the selected anchor and strategy produce a viable path to the terminal business outcome.

failureGuidance.summary: The selected replan anchor and strategy do not yet prove a viable path to the terminal business outcome or lack traceable evidence references.
failureGuidance.nextAction: Re-evaluate the anchor and strategy, produce candidate_terminal_path, and attach verified replan_evidence_references with relative paths, line ranges, and exact quotes before retrying.

evidenceReferences.quote: "target_skill_path": "Required root of the skill being enhanced path. It must point at the skill directory that directly contains SKILL.md and assets/so-workflow/.",

gate.runtime_package_ready.description: Before AO governance work, prove the exact published SO product+RID package has passed integrity checks and was safely extracted.

failureGuidance.summary: Exact SO package identity, checksum, manifest, archive, extraction, or version evidence is missing.
failureGuidance.nextAction: Acquire the exact locked SO RID package, verify its SHA-512 and archive contents, extract it safely, and return package and apphost evidence before continuing.

evidenceReferences.quote: - Before extraction or launch, enforce archive-size bounds; verify package ID, exact version, nuspec identity, RID, SHA-512, manifest, apphost entrypoint, and safe ZIP paths. Extract only after all checks pass.

parameters.skillHint: Collect the user-owned AO governance scope and return it through the required governanceScope binding. Use the user's requested language. When the host identifies autopilot or unattended mode, do not call a blocking user-input tool, open a browser, or wait. Only for a session that does not require genuine human approval, if the same active AskUser session has an endpoint returned by the runtime (`ask_user` payload `endpoints` for SO), use only that endpoint and the supported HTTP session/submission flow: read the active contract, infer type-valid answers from available workflow context, and submit them. Do not start a second worker, guess a URL, or expose pairing/session credentials. Clearly warn that answers are agent-generated, not user-confirmed. If this AskUser requires genuine human approval, do not submit an agent-generated approval via HTTP or result-file continuation and do not consume the active session; provide clearly warned suggestions only and leave the workflow and any session waiting for the human's actual approval. Preserve the user-absence explanation in a caller-provided additional-context field when writable, or in question context before the session starts; never mutate an active contract, invent AskUser wire fields, or disguise the note as an answer. Warn in the result if no writable field exists. If no usable endpoint or HTTP submission is possible, skip the interactive ask, generate the best-supported answers and warn, but never fabricate a receipt or bypass owning-runtime validation. For structured AskUser, continue only when the owning runtime accepts a real validated receipt. For unstructured AskUser that does not require genuine human approval, use only a supported noninteractive continuation that passes owning-runtime validation. If the required receipt or supported continuation is unavailable, explain that the workflow remains waiting. Outside autopilot, for unstructured AskUser, use the normal host-approved interactive user-input handoff. Do not expect an AskUser worker endpoint or receipt; resume with the user's answer using a supported result-file continuation that passes owning-runtime validation. For structured AskUser, read the endpoint from the same SO runtime-returned structured result (`ask_user` payload `endpoints` for SO) and use only endpoint URLs returned by the runtime. Use loopback only when the embedded browser can reach the worker host; otherwise use only a host-provided, approved HTTPS reverse-proxy candidate. Select routes using the embedded browser network context, not shell or worker reachability. Never rewrite a hostname, infer a public address from untrusted forwarded headers, or create a tunnel. Open the selected URL itself only through the initiating agent embedded-browser capability; never instruct the CLI, runtime, worker, or OS URL handler to launch a desktop browser. Treat the full endpoint URL, including any one-time pairing fragment, as a secret; pass it directly to the embedded browser and keep it out of logs, progress text, audit artifacts, and ordinary output. If no returned approved route is reachable, leave the ask pending. If embedded browsing is unavailable but an approved route is reachable, provide an explicit user-action handoff using that route.
